## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report out-of-sample realised risk and Sharpe for every covariance estimator against equal weighting on the same period.
- State the verdict, including the case where the simplest construction wins.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Run the full out-of-sample comparison: five constructions including equal weighting, reporting predicted risk, realised risk, the ratio, Sharpe with an interval, turnover and gross exposure. One table.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Interpret it correctly: a risk model earns its place by predicting realised risk accurately, not by producing the highest Sharpe, because the Sharpe comparison is dominated by the expected return estimate you already know is the weak input. Write that distinction into the milestone report and report both.
:::
